title: Frequency-dependent interaural cancellation did not improve initial foam-eyes-closed balance prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: In NHANES2001–2002 adults aged40–69 reaching balance condition4(n863), we fitted a frozen model and evaluated separately recruited NHANES2003–2004 participants(n799). Interaural cancellation across500,1000,2000,4000Hz did not establish added initial balance-failure prediction beyond nonlinear pure-tone averages and conventional covariates. Brier gain was -0.000504,500 source-target refit bootstrap95% interval[-0.003855,0.001147]. Linear/spline, measurement-quality and eventual-failure sensitivities did not show gains. Cross-sectional AI-authored exploratory analysis; not equivalence, causal vestibular inference or clinical validation.
